items.title: A Brazilian court fined lawyers $16k for a hidden prompt injection
items.summary: A hidden white-on-white instruction told Brazil's national court AI, Galileu, to go easy on a R$842,000 labor claim; Galileu flagged it and blocked the filing instead. The 3rd Labor Court of Parauapebas fined the two firms 10% of the claim, about $16,000, in what may be the first ruling worldwide on intentional prompt injection against a court AI. (4 minute read)

items.title: Google's Suncatcher satellite ran its first AI inference in orbit
items.summary: Google's Project Suncatcher prototype, launched October 1, powered up its TPU tray and ran Gemma 4 in orbit, producing a haiku that downlinked through a ground station over Svalbard. Follow-up prompts generated limericks and telemetry reports. No power or compute specs were disclosed; the next milestone is twin interconnected satellites in 2027. (3 minute read)

items.title: SynthID-style watermarking quietly cuts response diversity
items.summary: Claude's text watermarking, built on Google's SynthID-Text, biases token choice with a keyed pseudo-random sequence over a sliding window. SynthID's own supplement documents a diversity trade-off: one informal test found 4 of 5 watermarked responses to the same prompt opened nearly identically, versus 3 distinct openings unwatermarked. Key rotation cuts the effect but weakens detection on short text. (5 minute read)

items.title: mojo-dllm runs diffusion LLMs on CPU with no Python at runtime
items.summary: mojo-dllm is a from-scratch Mojo runtime for diffusion language models LLaDA-8B and Dream-7B, loading quantized GGUF weights with no Python at runtime. On a laptop CPU it hits 1.33 tokens/sec versus llama.cpp's 0.69; on an RTX 3050 it trails llama.cpp's CUDA path (9.43 vs 15.68 tokens/sec) but needs only about 1GB of host memory. (3 minute read)

items.title: Apollo economist: AI shows zero payoff outside Big Tech
items.summary: Apollo's chief economist Torsten Slok reports flat profit margins and revenue per worker across the S&P 493 - the S&P 500 minus Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Tesla - with no visible AI productivity gain. The note cites no underlying data, sample size, or time window. The debate over AI's ROI outside Big Tech now has a specific, if thin, data point to argue over. (2 minute read)

items.title: A hobbyist fine-tuned Qwen2.5-Code-7B into a demoscene-code model
items.summary: Demoscener-7B is Qwen2.5-Code-7B fine-tuned on 25k Dwitter 'Dweets' - 140-character JS demos - then refined with GRPO using the author's own ratings as the reward signal across roughly 40,000 reviewed animations. Perplexity on held-out Dweets dropped from 28.63 to 8.57 after pretraining and from 7.42 to 5.65 after curriculum training. Both the model and the 25k-Dweet dataset are open on Hugging Face. (6 minute read)

items.title: A language model runs straight from a 512-byte boot sector
items.summary: bootgpt loads an 11.5KB int8 model from 23 disk sectors and runs inference in 16-bit real mode on a 386-class CPU, with no OS and no C runtime. The character-level network, hand-written in x86 assembly, generates a fake Linux dmesg boot log using only integer multiplies and one division. The author's Python training simulation matches the assembly's output character for character. (3 minute read)

items.title: FreeVideo runs MiniMax H3 video generation on 8GB of VRAM
items.summary: FreeVideo is a local inference engine for MiniMax H3 video diffusion that streams weights in chunks to fit an 8GB-VRAM, 16GB-RAM consumer machine. Switching to int8 weights in v0.3.0 made 5-second clips generate about 2.3x faster on an RTX 3090. A preview build also runs on Apple silicon with 24GB of unified memory. (2 minute read)
